claim.operational_target: From exact reviewed public response events, build lineage-bound conditional public preference structures and route a new dialogue turn to direct evidence, an applicable repeated structure, related evidence without a new stance, or no person-specific prediction.
non_claims: LLM semantic candidates as verified evidence
calibrated real-person accuracy before temporal holdout evaluation
alternatives: generic topic overlap explains apparent transfer
the dialogue model supplies the apparent person stance
claim.scope: One public person; reviewed source spans, roles, audiences, declared domains, source lineages and evidence time. Generated dialogue is never fitting evidence.

identifiability.distinguishing_evidence: Strictly later reviewed real responses scored by the same V4 kernel and compared with direct-retrieval, wrong-person and duplicate-lineage baselines.
unidentified_questions: whether public responses reflect private mental states
whether undisclosed public records reverse a structure
whether observed public patterns remain stable outside the evidence window

evidence.completeness_boundary: The module verifies supplied bytes, exact reviewed spans, declared speaker, time and source lineage. It cannot prove corpus completeness, sincerity or hidden events.

computation.uncertainty_scope: Evidence support and applicability only; never an accuracy probability.

results.summary: 104 focused product and integration tests passed in 72.907 seconds

remaining_limitations: No adequate independent real-person temporal sample currently establishes prediction accuracy.
LLM event and query semantics remain bounded candidates; exact-span review and code gates cannot prove semantic truth.
General model knowledge is external briefing and never becomes person evidence without reviewed source material; ordinary non-numeric factual accuracy is not verified by code.
